children.text: āmāvāsyena vā paurṇamāsena vā haviṣā yakṣyamāṇo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When he is about to sacrifice with an oblation at the new moon or at the full moon,
he prepares beforehand the curdling substance for the oblation.
He does so one day before or two days before, according to the season.
Now there is also a brāhmaṇa statement.

children.text: dadhnātanakti sendratvāyāgnihotroccheṣaṇam abhyātanakti yajñasya saṃtatyā iti ||
children.translated_text: "He mixes it with curds for association with <s>Indra</s>; he mixes in the remains of the <s>agnihotra</s> for the continuity of the sacrifice," so it says.

children.text: candramasaṃ vānirjñāya sampūrṇaṃ vā vijñāyāgnīn anvādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having ascertained that the moon is not visible, or having known that it is full, he puts fuel on the fires.

children.text: trīṇi kāṣṭhāni gārhapatye 'bhyādadhāti trīṇy anvāhāryapacane trīṇy āhavanīye ||
children.translated_text: He lays three sticks on the <s>gārhapatya</s>, three on the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s>, and three on the <s>āhavanīya</s>.
They sweep around them.
They make the form of the fast-day rite.

children.text: athāsya vratopetasya parṇaśākhām ācchaiti prāṅ vodaṅ vā vācaṃyamo yatra vā vetsyan manyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, when he has undertaken the vow, he goes to cut a branch of a <s>parṇa</s> tree, facing east or north, keeping silent, wherever he thinks he will find one.

children.text: sā yā prācī vodīcī vā bahuparṇā bahuśākhāpratiśuṣkāgrā bhavati tām ācchinatti iṣe tvā ūrje tvā iti ||
children.translated_text: Whichever branch is eastward or northward, rich in leaves and many-branched, with its tip not withered, that he cuts, saying, "For refreshment I take you, for strength I take you."

children.text: tayā vatsān apākaroti vāyava stha upāyava stha iti ||
children.translated_text: With it he drives away the calves, saying, "You are winds; you are approachers."

children.text: athaiṣāṃ mātṝḥ prerayati devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatu śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇe āpyāyadhvam aghniyā devabhāgam ūrjasvatīḥ payasvatīḥ prajāvatīr anamīvā mā va stena īśata māghaśaṃso rudrasya hetiḥ pari vo vṛṇaktu iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he impels their mothers, saying, "May god <s>Savitṛ</s> set you in motion for the most excellent work. Swell, O inviolable ones, the gods' share, rich in nourishment, rich in milk, rich in offspring, free from disease. Let no thief rule over you, no evil-speaker; may <s>Rudra</s>'s missile avoid you."

children.text: dhruvā asmin gopatau syāta bahvīr iti yajamānam īkṣate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "Be steadfast under this lord of cattle, many in number," he looks at the sacrificer.

children.text: athaitāṃ śākhām agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya pūrvayā dvārā prapādya jaghanena gārhapatyam agniṣṭhe 'nasyuttarārdhe vāgnyagārasyodgūhati yajamānasya paśūn pāhi iti nu yadi saṃnayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, carrying that branch around in front of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, bringing it in by the eastern door, he hides it behind the <s>gārhapatya</s>, on the fire-place of the cart or in the northern half of the fire-house, saying, "Protect the sacrificer's cattle," but only if he performs the mixed-milk offering.

children.text: yady u vai na saṃnayati barhiḥ pratipad eva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not perform the mixed-milk offering, the first step is simply the barhis.

children.text: atha jaghanena gārhapatyaṃ tiṣṭhann asidaṃ vāśvaparśuṃ vādatte devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām ādade iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, standing behind the <s>gārhapatya</s>, he takes a sickle or a horse-axe, saying, "At the impulse of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I take you."
Having taken it, he addresses it, saying, "You are the sound of the sacrifice."

children.text: gārhapatye pratitapati pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayaḥ iti tris ||
children.translated_text: He heats it at the <s>gārhapatya</s>, saying three times, "Burnt away is the demon; burnt away are the enemies."

children.text: athāhavanīyam abhipraiti preyam agād dhiṣaṇā barhir accha manunā kṛtā svadhayā vitaṣṭā ta āvahanti kavayaḥ purastāt devebhyo juṣṭam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he goes toward the <s>āhavanīya</s>, saying, "The inspired thought has gone forward toward the barhis, made by <s>Manu</s>, spread out by its own power; the sages bring it in front, acceptable to the gods."

children.text: iha barhir āsade iti vediṃ pratyavekṣate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "Here may the barhis be seated," he looks down toward the altar.

children.text: atha tāṃ diśam eti yatra barhir vetsyan manyate ||
children.translated_text: Then he goes in the direction where he thinks he will find barhis grass.

children.text: darbhastambaṃ parigṛhṇāti yāvantam alaṃ prastarāya manyate devānāṃ pariṣūtam asi iti ||
children.translated_text: He takes hold of a clump of darbha grass, as much as he thinks sufficient for the prastara, saying, "You are enclosed for the gods."

children.text: athainam ūrdhvam unmārṣṭi varṣavṛddham asi iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he strokes it upward, saying, "You have grown by rain."

children.text: asidenopayacchati devabarhir mā tvānvaṅ mā tiryak parva te rādhyāsam iti ||
children.translated_text: With the sickle he draws it near, saying, "O divine barhis, may I not fail you lengthwise or crosswise at the joint."

children.text: ācchinatti ācchettā te mā riṣam iti ||
children.translated_text: He cuts it, saying, "May I, your cutter, not be harmed."

children.text: ācchedanāny abhimṛśati devabarhiḥ śatavalśaṃ viroha iti ||
children.translated_text: He touches the cuttings, saying, "O divine barhis, grow again with a hundred shoots."

children.text: sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhema ity ātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "May we grow apart with a thousand shoots," he touches himself.
He cuts that whole clump completely.

children.text: kṛtvā prastaraṃ nidadhāti pṛthivyāḥ saṃpṛcaḥ pāhi iti ||
children.translated_text: Having made the prastara, he sets it down, saying, "Protect the contacts of the earth."

children.text: tūṣṇīm ata ūrdhvam ayujo muṣṭīn lunoti ||
children.translated_text: From that point onward he silently cuts an odd number of handfuls.

children.text: trīn vā pañca vā sapta vā nava vaikādaśa vā yāvato vālaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: Three, or five, or seven, or nine, or eleven, or as many as he thinks sufficient.

children.text: atha trir anvāhitaṃ śulbaṃ kṛtvāpasalair āveṣṭayati adityai rāsnāsi iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made a cord with three successive turns, he wraps it with side-grasses, saying, "You are <s>Aditi</s>'s girdle."
Having laid it down with its tips toward the north,

children.text: tasmin prastaram abhisaṃbharati susaṃbhṛtā tvā saṃbharāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: he gathers the prastara into it, saying, "Well gathered, I gather you."
He binds it, saying, "The binding is for <s>Indrāṇī</s>."

children.text: granthiṃ karoti pūṣā te granthiṃ grathnātu iti ||
children.translated_text: He makes a knot, saying, "May <s>Pūṣan</s> tie your knot."

children.text: sa te māsthāt iti paścāt prāñcam upagūhati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "May it not stay on you," he tucks it in from behind toward the east.

children.text: athainad udyacchate indrasya tvā bāhubhyām udyacche iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he lifts it up, saying, "With <s>Indra</s>'s arms I lift you up."

children.text: śīrṣann adhinidhatte bṛhaspater mūrdhnā harāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: He places it on his head, saying, "With <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s head I carry it."
He goes, saying, "Follow the wide midspace."

children.text: etyottareṇa gārhapatyam anadhaḥ sādayati devaṃgamam asi iti ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to the north of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, he sets it down without lowering it, saying, "You are one that goes to the gods."

children.text: tad uparīva nidadhāti yatra guptaṃ manyate ||
children.translated_text: He lays it somewhat above, wherever he thinks it is protected.
He silently cuts the enclosing grasses.
For the Fathers he cuts what has been cut once.

children.text: atha tathaiva trir anvāhitaṃ śulbaṃ kṛtvaikaviṃśatidārum idhmaṃ saṃnahyati yat kṛṣṇo rūpaṃ kṛtvā prāviśas tvaṃ vanaspatīn tatas tvām ekaviṃśatidhā saṃbharāmi susaṃbhṛtā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the same way, after making a cord with three successive turns, he binds kindling wood of twenty-one sticks, saying, "When, having made the black form, you entered the forest trees, from there I gather you in twenty-one parts, well gathered."

children.text: vedaṃ karoti vatsajñuṃ paśukāmasya mūtakāryam annādyakāmasya trivṛtaṃ tejaskāmasyordhvāgraṃ svargakāmasya ||
children.translated_text: He makes the veda-bundle: from calf-knee grass for one desiring cattle, from mūta grass for one desiring work, threefold for one desiring food to eat, with upward tips for one desiring brilliance, and for one desiring heaven.
He makes the altar east of the northern enclosing stick.
Then in the afternoon he performs the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s>.
On the lion be my anger.
On the tiger be my internal disease.
On the wolf be my hunger.
On the horse be my voracity.
In the wilderness be my thirst.
In the king's house be my hunger for food.
On the stone be my lassitude.
On the donkey be my hemorrhoids.
On the porcupine be my shame.
On the aśvattha tree be my trembling.
On the tortoise be my disease of the limbs.
On the goat be my discharge disease.
On the disliked one be my death.
On the enemy be my evil.
On the rival be my destruction.
In ill repute be my decline.
On the envious one be my failure to prosper.
On the sword be my distress.
On the wild ox be my blindness.
On the gaur be my deafness.
On the bear be my grief.
On the iguana be my weariness.
On old age be my coldness.
On the black bird be my timidity.
On the whip be my evil smell.
On the owl be my dog-like ill fame.
On the clod be my jealousy.
On the monkey be my bad prosperity.
On the potter be my fleshiness.
On the howl be my brooding.
On the camel be my thirst.
On the antelope be my fatigue.
On the ewe be my sheepishness.
On the sheath be my smell.
On the maiden be my adornment.
On the boar be my dampness.
On the spotted snake be my dream.
On the python be my bad dream.
On the lightning be my false fame.
In greed be my moisture.
On the locust be my evil and misfortune.
Among women be my falsehood.
Among goats be my roughness.
On the vrātya be my calamity.
On the śūdra be my theft.
On the vaiśya be my improper act.
On the kinsman of a rājanya be my ignorance.
On the niṣāda be my brahmin-murder.
On the kuliṅga bird be my sneezing.
On the howl be my wantonness.
On the otter be my vomiting.
On the kiṃpuruṣa be my crying.
On the leopard be my burning away.
On the elephant be my leprosy.
On the dog be my foul impurity.
Among the sinewy ones be my barbarian speech.
Among the Videhas be my skin disease.
Among those of great rain be my lassitude.
Among the Mūjavants be my fever.
On the drum be my cough.
Among the Ikṣvākus be my bile.
Among the Kaliṅgas be my impurity.
On the she-mule be my childlessness.
On the courtesan be my bad conduct.
On the mouse be my tooth disease.
On the fly be my dog's mange.
On the parrot be my yellowness.
On the peacock be my chatter.
On the bull be my old age.
On the blue jay be my evil speech.
In the waters be my fatigue.
On the brahma-abandoner be my guilt.

children.text: apehi pāpman punar apanāśito bhava ā naḥ pāpman sukṛtasya loke pāpman dhehy avihṛto yo naḥ pāpman na jahāti tam u tvā jahimo vayam ||
children.translated_text: Go away, evil one; become driven away again. O evil one, place upon us, in the world of good deed, the one who is not separated from evil. O evil one, the one who does not leave us, him indeed we leave to you.

children.text: anyatrāsman niviśatām sahasrākṣo amartyo yo no dveṣṭi sa riṣyatu yam u dviṣmas tam u jahi iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the thousand-eyed, immortal one settle away from us. Let the one who hates us come to harm; and the one whom we hate, strike him down.

children.text: athāñjalināpa upahanti sumitrā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu iti ||
children.translated_text: Then with his joined hands he strikes the waters, saying, "May the waters and plants be good friends to us."

children.text: tāṃ diśam etā apa utsiñcati yasyām asya diśi dveṣyo bhavati durmitrās tasmai bhūyāsur yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti ||
children.translated_text: He pours out these waters toward that direction in which there is someone hateful to him, saying, "May they become bad friends to him who hates us and whom we hate."
Then, having touched the waters, they enter in the prescribed way.

children.text: yāvad evātrādhvaryuś ceṣṭati tāvad eṣa pratiprasthātā prāyaṇīyasya niṣkāsa udayanīyam abhinirvapati ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the adhvaryu is occupied there, this pratiprasthātṛ, at the refuse of the prāyaṇīya, prepares the udayanīya offering.

children.text: eṣa eva veda etan mekṣaṇam etad barhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The same veda-bundle is used, this same meṣaṇa, this same barhis.

children.text: athaitāṃ carusthālīṃ sakṣāmakāṣām utkhidya nirṇijya tayodayanīyaṃ śrapayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, having dug out and washed this caru-pot together with the charred remains, he cooks the udayanīya in it.

children.text: tasmiṃstathaiva śrapyamāṇe jaghanena gārhapatyam aupasadāyāṃ vedyāṃ stambayajur harati ||
children.translated_text: While it is being cooked in that same way, behind the gārhapatya, on the aupasada altar, he carries the stambayajus formula.
This is just the well-known procedure for the puroḍāśa.
Three times with a yajus formula, silently the fourth time.
He takes the former enclosing line.
He mutters the karaṇa formula.
They dig up.
From what has been dug up the āgnīdhra carries three times.
The rite is the same as for the prāyaṇīya.
This much alone is different.

children.text: pathyām amutra svastiṃ prathamāṃ yajati tām ihopottamāṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: There he offers Pathyā Svasti first; here he offers her next to last.
But the directions do not shift.

children.text: atha purastāt sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sruvāhutim upajuhoti yās te viśvāḥ samidhaḥ santy agne iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, before the sviṣṭakṛt, he offers with the sruva, saying, "Whatever universal kindling-sticks are yours, O Agni."
By the underlaying and the sprinkling over, they cut off this fixed ghee.
Some, however, offer the samiṣṭayajus.
With the śaṃyuvāka, the udayanīya comes to completion.
At this point he pours that full vessel inside the altar.

children.text: atha pṛṣadājyavanty ājyāni gṛhītvā maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām upākaroti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having taken ghee portions containing curdled ghee, he brings forward a Maitrāvaruṇa barren cow.

children.text: tasyai prasiddhaṃ vapayā caritvā dakṣiṇe vedyante keśaśmaśru vapate ||
children.translated_text: After performing the established procedure for its omentum, he shaves the hair and beard at the southern end of the altar.
He cuts the nails.
They perform the complete procedure for the animal.

children.text: atha yadi vaśāṃ na labhate maitrāvaruṇīm āmikṣāṃ gārhapatye śrapayitvā tayāhavanīye pracarati ||
children.translated_text: Then, if he does not obtain a Maitrāvaruṇa barren cow, after cooking āmikṣā on the gārhapatya, he proceeds with it on the āhavanīya.
It is completed with the portion for the ghee shares, the pratipat, and the iḍā-ending.
From that, in front of the āgnīdhra, he spreads out a hide-cutting in the iḍā-enclosure.
At the proper time the reciter cuts it across.

children.text: athaitau brāhmaṇaś ca śūdraś cāntareṇa sadohavirdhāne tiṣṭhata ārdraṃ carmakartam ādāya ||
children.translated_text: Then these two, a brahmin and a śūdra, stand between the sadas and the havirdhāna sheds, holding the moist hide-cutting.
The hotṛ mounts a swing.
The adhvaryu spreads out two bunches of grass, and the hotṛ priests spread out seats.
The udgātṛ ascends a seat made of udumbara wood.
He takes up a hundred-stringed lute.

children.text: āghāṭībhiḥ piñcholābhiḥ karkarīkābhir ity udgātāraṃ patnayaḥ paryupaviśanti ||
children.translated_text: The wives sit around the udgātṛ with cymbals, with fringed ornaments, and with little rattles.

children.text: atha dakṣiṇe vedyante kaṭaparivāre mithunau saṃpravādayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at the southern end of the altar, within a mat enclosure, a pair make music together.

children.text: athaitā dāsya udakumbhān adhinidhāya mārjālīyaṃ paryupaviśanti ||
children.translated_text: Then these servant women, having set down water jars, sit around the mārjālīya.

children.text: athādhvaryuḥ kūrcayor āsīno māhendrasya stotram upākaroti ||
children.translated_text: Then the adhvaryu, seated on the bunches of grass, begins the stotra for Mahendra.
They chant for Mahendra.

children.text: prastute sāmni saṃpraiṣam āha ājisṛta ājiṃ dhāvata dundubhīn samāghnata abhiṣotāro 'bhiṣuṇuta agnīd āśiraṃ vinayolūkhalam udvādaya pratiprasthātaḥ saumyasya viddhi iti ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Sāman</s> has begun, he gives the command: "O race-runners, run the race; beat the drums together; O pressers, press; O <s>Agnīdh</s>, bring down the mixture; O mortar, sound forth; O <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, pierce what belongs to Soma," thus.
They act according to the command.
The race-runners run.
They beat the drums.
They proclaim words together.

children.text: āghāṭībhiḥ piñcholābhiḥ karkarīkābhir ity udgātāraṃ patnaya upagāyanti ||
children.translated_text: With <s>āghāṭī</s> instruments, with <s>piñcholā</s> instruments, and with rattles, the wives sing in accompaniment to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.
